verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              अयं ते कर्ण सारथ्यं मद्रराजः करिष्यति । कृष्णादभ्यधिको यन्ता देवेशस्येव मातलिः ॥१॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said O Karna, this king of Madra, superior even to Krishna, will act as your driver, like Matali, the driver of the king of gods.

verses.sanskrit: यथा हरिहयैर्युक्तं संगृह्णाति स मातलिः । शल्यस्तथा तवाद्यायं संयन्ता रथवाजिनाम् ॥२॥
verses.english: As Matali manages his car drawn by the horse of Hari so will Shalya manage today your car and horses.

verses.sanskrit: योधे त्वयि रथस्थे च मद्रराजे च सारथौ । रथश्रेष्ठो ध्रुवं संख्ये पार्थानभिभविष्यति ॥३॥
verses.english: With you as the warrior on that car and the king of Madra as the charioteer it will, forsooth, defeat the Parthas in battle.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              ततो दुर्योधनो भूयो मद्रराजं तरस्विनम् । उवाच राजन्संग्रामेऽध्युषिते पर्युपस्थिते ॥४॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Thereupon again in the morning Duryodhana addressed the active king of

verses.sanskrit: कर्णस्य यच्छ संग्रामे मद्रराज हयोत्तमान् । त्वयाऽभिगुप्तो राधेयो विजेष्यति धनञ्जयम् ॥५॥
verses.english: O king of Madra, manage in battle the excellent horses of Karna. Protected by you Karna will defeat Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तो रथमास्थाय तथेति प्राह भारत । शल्येऽभ्युपगते कर्णः सारथिं सुमनाऽब्रवीत् ॥६॥
verses.english: Thus addressed he expressed his consent and got upon the chariot, O Bharata. When Shalya went there, Karna, in good spirits, addressed his driver saying, O charioteer, quickly equip this car for me.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं सूत स्यन्दनं मह्यं कल्पयेत्यसकृत्त्वरन् । ततो जैत्रं रथवरं गन्धर्वनगरोपमम् ॥७॥
विधिवत्कल्पितं भद्रं जयेत्युक्त्वा न्यवेदयत् । तं रथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कर्णोऽभ्यर्च्य यथाविधि ॥८॥
verses.english: How could Karna, that foremost of carwarriors, that powerful hero, that one of mighty prowess, was slain in battle by force by the son of Pritha?

verses.sanskrit: संपादितं ब्रह्मविदा पूर्वमेव पुरोधसा । कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं यत्नादुपस्थाय च भास्करम् ॥९॥
verses.english: Duly worshipping that car which had formerly been sanctified by a priest conversant with Brahma, going round it and worshipping the sun, Karna, the foremost of car-warriors, addressed the king of Madra, standing near him, saying-"get upon the chariot."

verses.sanskrit: समीपस्थं मद्रराजमारोह त्वमथाब्रवीत् । ततः कर्णस्य दुर्धर्षं स्यन्दनप्रवरं महत् ॥१०॥
आरुरोह महातेजाः शल्यः सिंह इवाचलम् । ततः शल्याश्रितं दृष्ट्वा कर्णः स्वं रथमुत्तमम् ॥११॥
verses.english: Then like a lion ascending a hill the highly energetic Shalya got upon the strong built car of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: अध्यतिष्ठद्यथाऽम्भोदं विद्युत्वन्तं दिवाकरः । तावेकरथमारूढावादित्याग्निसमत्विषौ ॥१२॥
verses.english: Beholding Shalya stationed there Karna got upon his most excellent car like the sun riding on a mass of clouds charged with lightning.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्राजेतां यथा मेघं सूर्याग्नी सहितौ दिवि । संस्तूयमानौ तौ वीरौ तदास्तां द्युतिमत्तमौ ॥१३॥
verses.english: Seated on the same car those two horses. effulgent like the sun and fire, shone there like the sun and fire sitting together on a cloud in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: ऋत्विक्सदस्यैरिन्द्राग्नी स्तूयमानाविवाध्वरे । स शल्यसंगृहीताश्वे रथे कर्णः स्थितो बभौ ॥१४॥
verses.english: Eulogised those two highly effulgent heroes shone like Indra and Agni (fire-god) adored with hymns in a sacrifice by Ritvikas and Sadasyas.

verses.sanskrit: धनुर्विस्फारयन् घोरं परिवेषीव भास्करः । आस्थितः स रथश्रेष्ठं कर्णः शरगभस्तिमान् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Shalya holding the reins of the horses Karna stood on that car stretching his dreadful bow like the sun enveloped with a circular light.

verses.sanskrit: प्रबभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रो मन्द्रस्थ इवांशुमान् । तं रथस्थं महाबाहुं युद्धायामिततेजसम् ॥१६॥
verses.english: Stationed on that best of cars Karna, the foremost of men, with the rays of his shafts, looked like the sun on the mount Mandara.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनस्तु राधेयमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् । अकृतं द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां दुष्करं कर्म संयुगे ॥१७॥
verses.english: Duryodhana invited to battle that mighty armed son of Radha of incomparable energy stationed on the car saying-O hero, O carwarrior, do you perform in the presence of all bond men an action, hard of accomplishment which had not been performed even by Bhishma and Drona.

verses.sanskrit: कुरुष्वाधिरथे वीर मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम् । मनोगतं मम ह्यासीद्भीष्मद्रोणौ महारथौ ॥१८॥
अर्जुनं भीमसेनं च निहन्ताराविति ध्रुवम् । ताभ्यां यदकृतं वीर वीरकर्म महामृधे ॥१९॥
verses.english: I had always thought that those two mighty car-warriors Bhishma and Drona would kill, without any doubt, Bhima and Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: तत् कर्म कुरु राधेय वज्रपाणिरिवापरः । गृहाण धर्मराजं वा जहि वा त्वं धनञ्जयम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Like the second wielder of thunderbolt do you accomplish that heroic feat in the great battle which had not been performed by them.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनं च राधेय माद्रीपुत्रौ यमावपि । जयश्च तेऽस्तु भद्रं ते प्रयाहि पुरुषर्षभ ॥२१॥
verses.english: Either attack the pious Yudhishthira or kill Arjuna and Bhima, O son of Radha and the twin sons of Madri.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्यानि कुरु सर्वाणि भस्मसात् । ततस्तूर्यसहस्राणि भेरीणामयुतानि च ॥२२॥
verses.english: Many blessings and victory attend you. Start for battle, O foremost of men, consume the arıny of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: वाद्यमानान्यराजन्त मेघशब्दो यथा दिवि । प्रतिगृह्य तु तद्वाक्यं रथस्थो रथसत्तमः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Ten thousands of trumpets and ten thousand drums simultaneously struck and produced a sound resembling the muttering of clouds in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यभाषत राधेयः शल्यं युद्धविशारदम् । चोदयाश्वान्महाबाहो यावद्धन्मि धनञ्जयम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: Accepting his words that foremost of carwarriors, the son of Radha stationed on the car, said to Shalya, an expert in fighting. Drive the horses on, O great heroes so that I may kill Arjuna, Bhima, the twins and Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनं यमौ चोभौ राजानं च युधिष्ठिरम् । अद्य पश्यतु मे शल्य बाहुवीर्यं धनञ्जयः ॥२५॥
अस्यतः कङ्कपत्राणां सहस्राणि शतानि च । अद्य क्षेप्स्याम्यहं शल्य शरान्परमतेजनान् ॥२६॥
verses.english: O Shalya, Arjuna will witness today the strength of my arms when I will discharge hundreds and thousands of Kanka feather were arrows.

verses.sanskrit:
पाण्डवानां विनाशाय दुर्योधनजयाय च । शल्य उवाच।
              सूतपुत्र कथं नु त्वं पाण्डवानवमन्यसे ॥२७॥
verses.english: I will shoot today, O Shalya, powerful arrows for destroying the Pandavas and securing victory for Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वास्त्रज्ञान्महेष्वासान् सर्वानेव महाबलान् । अनिवर्तिनो महाभागानजय्यान्सत्यविक्रमान् ॥२८॥
verses.english: Shalya said O son of a charioteer, why do you make light of the sons of Pandu who are all very powerful, great bow men and experts in the use of other weapons. They never retreat from battle, fortunate, unconquerable and are of great prowess.

verses.sanskrit: अपि सन्तनयेयुर्ये भयं साक्षाच्छतक्रतोः । यदा श्रोष्यसि निर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः ॥२९॥
verses.english: They are capable of striking fear even into the heart of Indra himself. O son of Radha, when you will hear the twang of his Gandiva bow in battle like the peal of the thunder itself you will not give vent to such words.

verses.sanskrit: राधेय गाण्डिवस्याजौ तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि । यदा द्रक्ष्यसि भीमेन कुञ्जरानीकमाहवे ॥३०॥
verses.english: When you will see Bhimsena killed elephants with their riders by serially splitting their teeth in the battle-field, your tongue will dcfinitely pause saying anything otherwise,

verses.sanskrit: विशीर्णदन्तं निहतं तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि । यदा द्रक्ष्यसि संग्रामे धर्मपुत्रं यमौ तथा ॥३१॥
शितैः पृषत्कैः कुर्वाणानभ्रच्छायामिवाम्बरे । अस्यतः क्षिण्वतश्चारीन् लघुहस्तान्दुरासदान् । पार्थिवानपि चान्यांस्त्वं तदा नैवं वदिष्यसि ॥३२॥
verses.english: When you will see Yudhishthira and the twins making a canopy with their sharpened shafts like that of clouds in the sky and other irrepressible kings all light-handed, shooting arrows reducing the number of their enemies you will not speak such words.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              अनादृत्य तु तद्वाक्यं मद्रराजेन भाषितम् । याहीत्येवाब्रवीत्कर्णो मद्रराजं तरस्विनम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Disregarding the words spoken by the king of Madra Karna said to him who was greatly active-"go on". Sanjaya said Disregarding the words spoken by the king of Madra Karna said to him who was greatly active-"go on".
